transcript:
This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,
or choose a guide with full service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take,
you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Lawmakers returned to Capitol Hill this week
as both parties prepare for a shift in power in January.
The midterms gave Democrats control of Congress
and expanded the party's reach in state governments.
NPR's Mara Liasson says the full scope of those gains
is still taking shape.
There's still more than a dozen races in the House
left to be called,
but the Democrats could have as big as an 80-seat majority
in the House next January.
And in the Senate, they have 54 seats now,
but Mississippi and Alaska are still left to be called,
and that could end up being 56 seats.
There are also six new Democratic state trifectas.
That means the Democrats will control
both legislative chambers and the governor's mansion.
In Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada,
Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin,
those are big states that are important
for the 2028 presidential elections.
That's NPR's Mara Liasson reporting.
Republicans will retain control of Congress
through the end of the year.
Lawmakers are facing a December deadline
to fund the government and avoid a shutdown.
Negotiations are expected to continue today
as hundreds of city workers in Portland, Oregon
prepare to strike on Monday.
Contract hawks have broken down over pay and job stability.
Union leader Carrie Koch says a walkout
could affect a wide range of services.
Our members are doing everything they can every day
to make the city high-functioning,
and we have to focus on that.
What can we do to provide services to Portlanders?
And what we can do is have skilled,
highly competent, capable workers at the helm
making that happen, and the way to do that
is a fair contract.
The planned walkout follows months
of contract negotiations with the city.
The union represents financial analysts,
administrative staff, and other office workers
across city agencies.
Israel is taking a step toward possibly
ousting its longest-serving leader, Benjamin Netanyahu's
top rival has been tapped to form the next government.
NPR's Lauren Frere reports Gadi Isincott
is facing a number of challenges in putting together
the next governing coalition.
Gadi Isincott is a former Israeli military chief
whose soldier son was killed in combat in Gaza.
He briefly served in Prime Minister Netanyahu's cabinet
before quitting, forming a new party, and challenging him.
Neither man won a majority in last month's election,
but most other parties have said
they want Isincott to govern.
He's got to build a coalition, though, first,
which could include Arab-led parties.
Palestinian citizens of Israel voted in record numbers.
It could also include ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties,
which are demanding exemption from military service.
Isincott has about six weeks to form a government
during which Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister
and could try to thwart his efforts.
Lauren Frere, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
This is NPR News.
Ukrainian, Russian, and American negotiators
are scheduled to meet in Abu Dhabi Tuesday and Wednesday.
The talks will focus on ending the war in Ukraine,
security arrangements, and humanitarian measures.
The meeting comes as Russia steps up a tax
on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
The Department of Justice is suing Penn State
over its tuition policy on undocumented residents.
The university is one of 27 institutions and states
that the DOJ has targeted with lawsuits.
And Danahe from member station WPSU reports.
Penn State's policy states undocumented students
can be eligible for in-state tuition
if they meet the university's residency requirements.
That includes going to a Pennsylvania high school
for at least four years.
But the U.S. Department of Justice says the policy
unconstitutionally discriminates against U.S. citizens
who don't get the same reduced rate.
Gabby Pacheco, president and CEO of TheDream.US,
said the students affected by the lawsuits
are not outsiders.
They're students who grew up right here in our backyards,
in our country, in our communities,
and they are embedded in our states.
That organization gives undocumented students scholarships
and argues in-state tuition expands access to higher education
and supports state and local economies.
In State College, I'm Ann Danahe.
The latest report on consumer prices is due out on Tuesday.
The figures will offer a fresh look
at how quickly prices are rising.
This is NPR.
This message comes from Cure Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community,
connections and the memories they make are everything.
Cure Alzheimer's Fund empowers scientists
pursuing bold Alzheimer's research.
